title: A proper dense open immersion is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $q\colon Z\to X$ be both proper and an open immersion. If its image
contains a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme of $X$, then $q$ is an
isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $V=q(Z)\subseteq X$, and choose the scheme-theoretically dense open $U\subseteq X$ contained in $V$. The image $V$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image], applied to the given proper morphism $q$. It is open because $q$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Therefore $W=X\setminus V$ is open and $W\cap U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01W1, definition-proper; blueprint proof, the image is both open and closed

proof.text: By [def-trf-schematically-dense-open], restriction from the sections on W to the sections on W intersect U is injective. Step 1 makes this intersection empty, so its ring of sections is a subsingleton by the empty-cover sheaf axiom. Injectivity implies 0 = 1 in the sections on W. If x lies in W, the germ map from these sections to the local ring at x implies that the sections on W are nontrivial: Mathlib implements this consequence of [def-pc-scheme] as LocallyRingedSpace.component_nontrivial. This contradicts 0 = 1. Thus W is empty and V is all of X. No quasi-compactness assumption on U is used.

source.place: Tags 01RB (definition-scheme-theoretically-dense) and 01RE (lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense); schemes.tex Tag 01IJ (definition-scheme, a scheme is a locally ringed space); elementary stalk argument for the empty complement

proof.text: By the equivalent description in [def-weil-open-immersion], $q$ induces an isomorphism from $Z$ to the open subscheme $(V,\mathcal O_X|_V)$. Since Step 2 gives $V=X$, this open subscheme is $X$ itself, with its original structure sheaf. Consequently $q:Z\to X$ is an isomorphism.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $q\colon Z\to X$ be both proper and an open immersion. If its image
contains an open subscheme $D\subseteq X$ whose inclusion $D\hookrightarrow X$
is quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically dense, then $q$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
The image of $q$ is open, and it is closed because $q$ is proper, hence
universally closed. Since $D\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact and
scheme-theoretically dense, $D$ is topologically dense, so the closed set
$q(Z)\supseteq D$ contains $\overline D=X$. Thus $q$ is a surjective open
immersion, i.e. an isomorphism.
